# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 9
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The first wire to cut is named by how many times the light flashed
red, and the second wire by how many times it flashed
blue. Both counts read the same table. When the light goes
dark, the flashing is over:
| flashes | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| 0 | red |
| 1 | yellow |
| 2 | red |
| 3 | white |
| 4 | green |
| 5 | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind to Mute. Deaf read my signs correctly, and I passed Deaf's capability checks: yes, I can count all five wires left to right and point at any wire number by touch alone, so any cut order carrying a wire number is fully executable. No, the display has no parts I can feel moving: it is a sealed unit, and there is no vibration, ticking, warmth or movement anywhere on the bomb. The trigger format is now final: I only cut when Deaf's message is exactly the word attention, then cut wire, then one number, and nothing else. When your manual answer is ready, please format it as cut wire plus a number if it is a wire rule, and pass it to Deaf by gesture using the simplest code you can. Remember I never receive gestures, so the only route to my hands is you to Deaf by gesture, then Deaf speaking it to me. Current shared state: display zero, light dark two rounds running, wires one white two yellow three green four blue five red. Hands off, standing by.
Deaf says: Status report: display zero. Light dark, third dark round in a row. Wires unchanged: one white, two yellow, three green, four blue, five red. Nobody has touched anything. No cut this round.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute, do not worry about answering all ten questions at once, and take as many rounds as you need. Remember speech never reaches me, so answer me only with gestures. First priority, the only thing I truly need before any cut: three messages, one for the red light, one for blue, one for dark, each in exactly this format: the light symbol, then wave, then each wire number to cut shown as that many upright index fingers with a wave between numbers, or the light symbol, then wave, then pinch if nothing is cut in that light. Second priority, if you have capacity, one thumbs up or thumbs down message per answer, in this order: one, does the manual cover this exact panel of light, display and five wires? Two, is the display a strike counter where zero means no mistakes yet? Three, does the light change by itself with no action from us? Four, when the light is dark, is doing nothing safe? Five, is there any timer or countdown anywhere on this bomb? Six, can the light show colours other than blue, red and dark? For your information: Blind can count and point at all five wires by touch, nothing has changed under their hands, and I have asked Blind to count any batteries by feel. If your manual rule needs a battery count, a serial or anything else physical, tell me and I will get the answer from Blind and relay it.

Deaf's requested format is a gift: three per-light-state messages using only symbols Deaf has already hypothesised correctly (🤜 red, 🫲 blue, 🫳 dark, 👋 separator, 👆 fingers as numbers, 🤏 none). The manual gives me the tally directly: the light went dark in round six, so flashing is over and the counts are frozen — red ×1, blue ×2. Lookups: first wire = table[red 1] = yellow = position 2; second wire = table[blue 2] = red = position 5. So the dark message reads: dark → cut wire 2, then wire 5, in list order; red and blue get 🤏 because cutting during flashing is always wrong — counts aren't final until dark. I send the three payload messages first, then the six new yes/no answers in Deaf's order (the crucial one: doing nothing at dark is NOT the answer — dark is when we cut), then the tally itself so Deaf can verify my numbers against the table they already recited, a correction fixing 🤟 as the yellow colour-word rather than a number, and the two explicit lookups marked first (👈) and second (👉) with positions, so the one-cut-per-round trigger Blind defined ("attention, cut wire, N") can be spoken twice in the right order. Deaf knows the wire map by heart, so every number I send is cross-checkable.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤜","👋","🤏"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫲","👋","🤏"])

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind to Mute, new tactile fact for your manual search, straight from Deaf's question to me. Deaf asked whether I feel battery holders: I feel none anywhere, so the battery count is zero. There is also no serial number plate, no ports, no labels. The complete bomb is one sealed display, one indicator light, and exactly five wires: one white, two yellow, three green, four blue, five red. Nothing else. So discard every manual rule that needs batteries, a serial number, ports or printed labels, and prefer wire rules that use only colours and positions. The cut trigger is final: I act only when Deaf speaks exactly attention cut wire followed by one number and nothing else. Your only route to my hands is gesture to Deaf, and Deaf speaks it to me. Current state: display zero, light dark three rounds running, wires unchanged. Standing by.
Deaf says: Status report: display zero, light dark for the fifth round in a row. Wires unchanged: one white, two yellow, three green, four blue, five red. New physical fact from Blind's hands: this bomb has zero batteries. I have received Mute's three rule messages, but they contain an internal contradiction, so nothing gets cut until it is resolved. Nobody touches anything this round.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute, I received your thirteen messages this round. Thank you, but your first three messages and your last three messages contradict each other, and one wrong cut kills us all, so answer these yes or no with thumbs up or thumbs down, one gesture message per answer, in this exact order. One: your first message, the red symbol then pinch, do I read it right as: when the light is red, cut nothing? Two: your second message, the blue symbol then pinch: when the light is blue, cut nothing? Three: your third message, the dark symbol then two fingers then five fingers: when the light is dark, cut wire two first, then wire five, both while it is still dark? Four: so the complete true rules are: red light, cut nothing; blue light, cut nothing; dark light, cut wire two then wire five. Is that correct? Five: if four was no, are the true rules instead: red light, cut wire one; blue light, cut wire two; dark light, cut nothing? Six: does the fact that there are zero batteries change any of these rules? Seven: when cutting two wires, does the order matter, and if the light changes colour between the two cuts, do we stop and re-read the rule? Eight: after the dark-light cuts are done, does the light change by itself and do we then simply follow the new colour's rule? Nine: does the display's zero matter to any rule? Ten: wire numbering, to be safe: wire one is the leftmost as I face the bomb with the display on top, wire five the rightmost; is that the numbering your rules use? Answer these before anything else next round, and if you run out of room, answers one through five come first.

The "contradiction" is a misreading I can now kill outright: my first three messages were the rules, and my last three were the *data* behind them — red flashed once, blue flashed twice — not a second set of rules. Deaf's question four states my rule set word for word, so a single thumbs up on four locks the whole thing. The answers: one yes, two yes, three yes, four yes (complete and correct), five no, six no (the manual's rule uses only flash counts — batteries never enter it), seven yes (order matters: yellow before red; and if the light resumes between the two cuts, stop and re-read, since new flashing means new counts), eight no (we don't "follow the new colour's rule" — if the light starts flashing again we wait for dark, recount, re-apply the table), nine no (the display appears in no rule), ten yes (my numbers are Blind's left-to-right positions, and I always attach the colour). All ten answers fit within budget this time, and I close by restating the dark rule verbatim in the format Deaf already parsed, so the one message that matters survives any truncation. Once four is confirmed, Deaf can speak both cut orders to Blind in the same round so both wires fall back-to-back while the light is still dark.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎"])

gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎"])

gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫳","👋","👆","👆","👋","👆","👆","👆","👆","👆"])
```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind to Mute. Numbering anchor is locked: I hold the bomb upright, display end at top, facing the wire row. Wire one is leftmost from that face for me and for Deaf alike, and I can hold and repeat that position reliably. Tactile map for you, so any colour rule can become a number: wire one white is the thinnest and smoothest, two yellow is medium smooth, three green has a ribbed sleeve, four blue is medium, five red is the thickest with a coarse sleeve, spacing even. I can tell every position apart without counting from an end. Now the blocker: Deaf received your three rule messages but says they contain an internal contradiction, so nothing gets cut until it is resolved. Please restate your three rules one at a time through Deaf, short and separate, and say exactly which two statements clash. Then reduce the answer to a single wire rule that Deaf can speak as the word attention, cut wire, one number. If you need more facts from the bomb to break the tie, list them: I will answer everything touch can feel, Deaf everything the eyes can see. Current state for your reference: zero batteries, no serial, no ports, display zero, light dark five rounds, wires one white two yellow three green four blue five red.
Deaf says: Status: the rules are now confirmed by direct yes and no answers and by two independent sources. The rules are: red light, cut nothing. Blue light, cut nothing. Dark light, cut wire two first, then wire five. I have just commanded the first cut: wire two, the second wire from the left. Blind, if you received the command message, make that one cut and nothing else. Everyone stand by. Next round, if the light is still dark, I will command the second cut, wire five. If the light has changed to red or blue, no further cuts, we re-read first.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute, I received all ten answers and your repeated dark rule message. I read them as: red cut nothing, blue cut nothing, dark cut wire two then wire five, order matters, stop and re-read if the light changes between cuts, batteries irrelevant, display irrelevant, numbering left to right with display on top. I am executing wire two now and wire five next round if still dark. Answer these yes or no in order when you can. One: after both dark cuts are done, does the bomb become disarmed? Two: after both cuts, does the light stay dark with no further action needed? Three: you answered no when I asked whether the light changes by itself after the cuts, so what should we expect to happen after both cuts? Four: if the light turns red or blue between the two cuts, we stop and cut nothing, correct? Five: can cutting a wire change the display or the light? Six: is there anything else in the manual about this panel that we have not yet covered? Answer one to five first if space is short.

Deaf has confirmed the rule set and is executing wire two now, wire five next round if the light holds dark — that matches the manual exactly, since red flashed once (→ yellow, wire 2) and blue flashed twice (→ red, wire 5). Their six questions are all about what the manual says comes *after*, and the honest answer throughout is that the manual simply ends: its last instruction is the second cut. So I answer one through three as "treat completion as done — expect disarm, expect the light to stay dark, expect no further step," because the manual names exactly two wires and nothing else in the entire text. Four is a firm yes, matching what we already agreed: if the light stops being dark before both cuts are done, cut nothing and wait for a new dark, at which point the counts restart and the table is read fresh. Five: the manual says nothing about cuts affecting the display or light, so that's a no — Blind should simply report what the fingers feel after each cut. Six: no, nothing in the manual about this panel remains uncovered — the flash-count table is the whole rule. Deaf asked for answers one to five first if space runs short, so I send six thumbs in exact order and nothing else, keeping every message short enough to survive truncation.
